items.followUp: State the difference between aerobic and anaerobic respiration.

rubric.why: Cellular respiration involves the breakdown or oxidation of glucose in cells.
rubric.description: Defines cellular respiration as the breakdown or oxidation of glucose in cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying glucose as being broken down or oxidised.

rubric.why: Respiration releases energy that the cell can use.
rubric.description: States that cellular respiration releases energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the release of energy.

modelAnswer: Cellular respiration is the series of reactions in cells in which glucose is broken down.
This process releases energy for the cell.

items.followUp: Write the word equation for photosynthesis.

rubric.why: The definition identifies the organisms, raw materials, energy source and food produced in photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Explains that plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the process, reactants, energy source and product.

rubric.why: The balanced equation shows the reactants and products in the correct proportions and indicates the conditions.
rubric.description: Writes the balanced chemical equation for photosynthesis with light and chlorophyll indicated.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation and indication of light and chlorophyll.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.

rubric.why: Alcoholic fermentation is an anaerobic process commonly carried out by yeast.
rubric.description: States that yeast breaks down glucose in the absence of oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying yeast and the absence of oxygen.

rubric.why: Ethanol and carbon dioxide are the products that identify alcoholic fermentation.
rubric.description: Identifies ethanol and carbon dioxide as the products.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both products or giving their chemical formulae.

modelAnswer: In the absence of oxygen, yeast breaks down glucose by alcoholic fermentation.
